clue.text: Cave worker admits fighting

definitions.note: Latin for 'look out!', used as a warning cry at English public schools

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the worker insect takes the fighting word inside it

parts.note: a worker is a bee, the sterile female of the hive
fighting is war

explanation.surface: A miner or potholer underground lets slip that there has been a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave' is not a hollow in rock but the Latin imperative 'cave!', schoolboy slang for 'look out!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are warnings telling someone to be on guard; the Latin imperative translates as the English command.

clue.text: Follower of a Jul 31 rising is a lizard

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top, so these letters are turned round

parts.note: the day after 'a Jul 31' is 'an Aug 1': the article changes too, AN AUG I

explanation.surface: Something that comes after the last day of July turns out to be a reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: The follower of 'a Jul 31' is 'an Aug 1', the article changing with the vowel; 'rising' turns ANAUGI round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical American reptile of the family Iguanidae.

clue.text: Swinger on a trapeze shaft coming to grief?

indicators.note: coming to grief means meeting with disaster, so the letters of these words are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A trapeze artist on the bar has an accident with the shaft giving way.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Rice Burroughs's jungle hero famously travels by swinging from vine to vine.

clue.text: Learned to dodge Latin repeat

indicators.note: to dodge means to avoid, so the abbreviation for Latin is left out of the learned word

parts.note: learned means literate, well-read

explanation.surface: An educated person avoids Latin and simply says things again.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to do or say something over again, a direct synonym of repeat as a verb.

clue.text: Accept bribe to continue rallying?

definitions.meaning: a backhander is slang for a bribe, so to take one is to accept it
in tennis a rally goes on if a player plays the ball back on the backhand

explanation.surface: Someone is offered a bribe in order to keep a political rally going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rallying' suggests politics or recovery, but the second sense is a tennis rally.
explanation.definitionFit: Backhander is British slang for an illicit payment, and also a tennis stroke played across the body.

clue.text: Green-eyed one puts down electronic shutter

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something down sends it to the bottom, so that letter moves to the end

parts.note: green-eyed means jealous, from Shakespeare's green-eyed monster
one is the Roman numeral I
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A jealous person disparages an electronic window blind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts down' looks like belittling, but it moves the E of JEALOUSI to the bottom of the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalousie is a window blind or shutter of angled slats, the French word literally meaning jealousy.

clue.text: 'Neither shy nor outgoing', expressed verbatim

indicators.note: expressed in the sense of squeezed out, so the letters of the following word are pressed into new shape

explanation.surface: A quoted description of someone's personality, repeated word for word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressed' seems to mean spoken, but it means pressed out, rearranging VERBATIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychologists use this term for a personality balanced between introvert and extrovert traits.

clue.text: Arresting one East German star getting out of order

indicators.note: out of order means disarranged, so the letters of these three words are shuffled

explanation.surface: A celebrity from the old GDR behaves badly and is detained.
explanation.definitionFit: In Parliament this officer keeps order and can take an unruly member into custody.

clue.text: See 8
5.25 days? I'm scared!

indicators.note: 5.25 days is three quarters of seven, so only three of the four letters of the period are kept

parts.note: seven days make a week

explanation.surface: A long stretch of time prompts a frightened yelp.
explanation.walkthrough: 5.25 days is three-quarters of a week, so a quarter of the four-letter word is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: This interjection is a cry of fright, the sort of squeak someone makes when alarmed.

clue.text: Unpleasant condition king prepared with extremists of Arabia

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
a la, as in a dish prepared in a certain style
A and Z are the two extremes of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A ruler makes ready alongside Arabian radicals, an unpleasant situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists' are not militants but A to Z, the ends of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tropical disease, visceral leishmaniasis, spread by sandflies: a decidedly nasty illness.

clue.text: Former lover in audition from a foreign country

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
otic means relating to the ear, the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: An old flame turns up at a casting session, having come from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' is not a tryout but the sense of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotic originally meant introduced from abroad, not native, before its sense of strikingly unusual.

clue.text: The jury's out on the Body Worlds exhibition?

definitions.meaning: an idiom meaning nothing has been decided yet
Body Worlds is a touring show of preserved human corpses, dead bodies on display

explanation.surface: No verdict yet on the controversial show of plastinated human bodies.
explanation.walkthrough: Body Worlds is Gunther von Hagens's touring exhibition of preserved corpses, so it shows human remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means still undecided, and read literally describes corpses put on view.

clue.text: Second/first person expressed pretension!

parts.note: a mo is a moment, as in 'wait a second'
I is the first person singular pronoun

explanation.surface: A grammar note listing second and first person, said with airs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks grammatical but is a short time, MO.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for me is used jokingly, as Miss Piggy does, to signal mock vanity or affectation.

clue.text: Leave quietly, relieved of female underwear

definitions.meaning: to go away unnoticed, to sneak out
a slip is a woman's undergarment

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks away after removing her petticoat.
explanation.walkthrough: The trap is to remove an F ('female') from something; instead the phrase describes taking off a slip.
explanation.definitionFit: To sneak away unobtrusively is a standard idiom for departing without fuss.

clue.text: Man's gone off crime, which causes hilarity

indicators.note: gone off means departed, so these letters leave the crime word

parts.note: manslaughter is the crime of unlawful killing without intent
taken as the letters MANS

explanation.surface: A reformed criminal's change of heart is a source of amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilarity is loud merriment, the noise of people finding something very funny.

clue.text: Old pro I fancy carries a picture

indicators.note: carries means holds within, so the scrambled letters enclose the article
fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A veteran professional photographer admires an image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges OLD PRO I into POLROID, which 'carries' A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The trade name for an instant camera also names the snapshot print it produces.

clue.text: Holt-dweller not quite over ECT treatment group

indicators.note: over means covering, so the shortened animal word sits around the other letters
not quite means missing the very end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a holt is an otter's den

indicators.note: treatment means working over, so these three letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An otter is said to be undergoing electroconvulsive therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: A holt is an otter's riverbank den; ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, here only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of eight performers or things, the variant spelling of octet.

clue.text: Couple at work rejecting rescue vehicle

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing out, so the letters of the vessel leave the phrase

parts.note: taken as written; the three surviving letters run together in it only by coincidence, since the parse removes the vessel's letters rather than hiding a word
Noah's ark saved the animals from the Flood

explanation.surface: Two colleagues on the job turn down an ambulance or lifeboat.
explanation.walkthrough: The A, R and K come out of ATWORK separately, leaving the other three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is a pair, two of something.

clue.text: Turn up with e.g. dog in race

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the animal word sits within the arrival word

parts.note: to come is to arrive or turn up
a dog is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: Someone arrives with a greyhound to enter it in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: To race is to contend against others for a prize, the verb sense matching.

clue.text: Reply to "I don't fancy yours much!"? I don't believe it

definitions.text: Reply to "I don't fancy yours much!"?
definitions.meaning: if someone dislikes one of your legs, you invite them to tug the second
an expression of disbelief, short for 'you're kidding me'

explanation.surface: A sharp retort to a slighting remark, then an exclamation of disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull the other one, it's got bells on' is a British retort to a leg-pull; literally one leg is being disparaged.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells a joker you are not taken in, the follow-on to 'pulling my leg'.

clue.text: Hurry up with a ball application

definitions.meaning: a call for something awaited to come quickly
deodorant applied from a container with a rolling ball

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get a move on with an entry for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' suggests a dance; it is the rolling ball in a deodorant dispenser.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a wish for time to pass, and a ball-tipped applicator product.

clue.text: On the sniff? Please don't serenade me!

definitions.meaning: pushing the nose in, investigating by smell
read as two words, a refusal of any song

explanation.surface: A sniffing suitor is told not to sing under the window.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer into two words, a request for no singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Poking the snout about, sniffing, is what a dog does when following a scent.

clue.text: Task anticipating a nervous condition

indicators.note: anticipating means coming before, so the task word precedes the article

parts.note: a chore is a routine task

explanation.surface: Someone dreads a job, expecting it to bring on anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nervous condition' suggests anxiety; it is a disorder of the nervous system.
explanation.definitionFit: This disorder, St Vitus's dance, causes involuntary jerky movements and is neurological.

clue.text: Emotional pain a thing of the past for this optimist?

parts.note: a pang is a sudden sharp feeling of distress
something lost is gone, now in the past

explanation.surface: Someone who has stopped feeling hurt must be a confirmed optimist.
explanation.walkthrough: Pangloss is the relentlessly cheerful tutor in Voltaire's Candide.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltaire's doctor insists all is for the best in the best of all possible worlds, a byword for optimism.

clue.text: Confusion that is easy

definitions.meaning: in printing, ... is type jumbled together, a muddle

explanation.surface: Muddle, it's said, is a simple matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers call mixed-up type pie, and the phrase 'easy as pie' gives the second sense.

clue.text: As irrelevant as decimal place #1?

definitions.meaning: not pertinent to the matter in hand
the first decimal place sits right next to the decimal point

explanation.surface: Something deemed as pointless as an obscure mathematical detail.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means off the subject, and literally places the first digit after the dot.

clue.text: See 27
